help.long:
cmw makes git worktrees fast to create, cheap on disk, and safe to clean up.
Built for humans and AI agents running many worktrees in parallel.

  - Dependencies (node_modules, Pods, vendor, ...) are copy-on-write cloned from the main
    checkout: ready in seconds, almost no extra disk.
  - .env, local.properties, keystores and other ignored secrets follow every worktree.
  - Node, iOS, Android, Expo/React Native, PHP, Python, Rust out of the box.
  - Cleanup removes merged worktrees plus their DerivedData, .cxx, build caches.

Agent-friendly by design:
  --json or CMW_JSON=1   one JSON document on stdout: {ok, command, data, warnings} or {ok:false, error:{kind,message,hint}}
  never prompts          destructive commands are dry runs unless --yes / --force
  fix hints              every refusal includes the exact command that resolves it
  idempotent             re-running new/hydrate is safe; `cmw new <branch>` returns the existing path
  exit codes             0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 refused (unsafe), 4 not found
  parallel-safe          a repo-wide lock serializes concurrent cmw runs

Usage: cmw [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  new              Create a worktree for <branch> and hydrate it. Prints the path as the last line
  hydrate          Bring deps (clone), secrets (copy) and envs (regen) from the main checkout into a worktree
  ls               List worktrees with branch, dirty state, merge state, age
  path             Print the path of a worktree (by branch, slug, dir name or path)
  rm               Remove a worktree, its build caches and (if merged) its branch
  gc               Find and remove merged, clean worktrees. Dry run unless --yes
  clean-artifacts  Delete regenerable caches (DerivedData, .cxx, build, .next, ...) from idle worktrees. Dry run unless --yes
  env              Manage copied secrets/config (.env, local.properties, ...)
  shell-init       Print shell integration (adds `cmw cd <name>`). Use: eval "$(cmw shell-init zsh)"
  agents           Set up coding agents: skills for Claude Code, Codex and Grok, Claude Code hooks, and a setup prompt to paste
  skill            Install the cmw skill (same as `cmw agents install`) or print an AGENTS.md snippet
  update           Upgrade cmw to the latest release (Homebrew, installer or cargo). --check only reports
  hook             Claude Code worktree hooks: print the snippet or merge it into settings.json (see also `cmw agents`)
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json
          Emit a single JSON document on stdout (also: CMW_JSON=1)
          
          [env: CMW_JSON=]

  -C <DIR>
          Run as if started in this directory (like `git -C`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

new.long:
Create a worktree for <branch> and hydrate it. Prints the path as the last line

Usage: cmw new [OPTIONS] <BRANCH>

Arguments:
  <BRANCH>  Branch to check out. Created from --base if it doesn't exist

Options:
      --base <BASE>  Base ref for a new branch. Default: origin/<default-branch> if present, else <default-branch>
      --json         Emit a single JSON document on stdout (also: CMW_JSON=1) [env: CMW_JSON=]
  -C <DIR>           Run as if started in this directory (like `git -C`)
      --path <PATH>  Where to create the worktree. Default: ~/.cmw/worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug> ($CMW_HOME overrides ~/.cmw)
      --fetch        `git fetch origin` before creating the branch
      --no-hydrate   Only create the worktree; don't hydrate
      --no-install   Never run package managers (clone/copy only)
      --no-slow      Skip slow installers (pod install); they are reported as `needs_setup`
  -h, --help         Print help

hydrate.long:
Bring deps (clone), secrets (copy) and envs (regen) from the main checkout into a worktree

Usage: cmw hydrate [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  Worktree to hydrate. Default: the current one

Options:
      --from <FROM>  Source checkout. Default: the repo's main checkout
      --json         Emit a single JSON document on stdout (also: CMW_JSON=1) [env: CMW_JSON=]
  -C <DIR>           Run as if started in this directory (like `git -C`)
      --dry-run      Show what would happen without changing anything
      --no-install   Never run package managers (clone/copy only)
      --no-slow      Skip slow installers (pod install); they are reported as `needs_setup`
  -h, --help         Print help

ls.long:
List worktrees with branch, dirty state, merge state, age

Usage: cmw ls [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --all    List worktrees of every repo found under ~/.cmw/worktrees, ~/.t3/worktrees and $CMW_SCAN_ROOTS
      --json   Emit a single JSON document on stdout (also: CMW_JSON=1) [env: CMW_JSON=]
  -C <DIR>     Run as if started in this directory (like `git -C`)
      --sizes  Include apparent disk size per worktree (slower; clones are counted at full size)
  -h, --help   Print help

Remove a worktree, its build caches and (if merged) its branch

Usage: cmw rm [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Branch, branch slug, directory name, or path

Options:
      --force        Remove even with uncommitted changes or unpushed, unmerged commits (destroys that work)
      --json         Emit a single JSON document on stdout (also: CMW_JSON=1) [env: CMW_JSON=]
  -C <DIR>           Run as if started in this directory (like `git -C`)
      --keep-branch  Keep the branch even if it is merged
      --dry-run      Show what would be removed
  -h, --help         Print help

gc.long:
Find and remove merged, clean worktrees. Dry run unless --yes

Usage: cmw gc [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json          Emit a single JSON document on stdout (also: CMW_JSON=1) [env: CMW_JSON=]
      --yes           Actually remove. Without it, gc only reports
  -C <DIR>            Run as if started in this directory (like `git -C`)
      --stale <DAYS>  Also report worktrees with no commits for this many days (never auto-removed)
      --all           Every repo under the scan roots, not just the current one
  -h, --help          Print help

clean-artifacts.long:
Delete regenerable caches (DerivedData, .cxx, build, .next, ...) from idle worktrees. Dry run unless --yes

Usage: cmw clean-artifacts [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --idle <DAYS>  Only worktrees with no commits or file changes for this many days [default: 7]
      --json         Emit a single JSON document on stdout (also: CMW_JSON=1) [env: CMW_JSON=]
  -C <DIR>           Run as if started in this directory (like `git -C`)
      --yes          Actually delete. Without it, only reports
      --all          Every repo under the scan roots, not just the current one
  -h, --help         Print help

output.shell-init zsh:
cmw() {
  if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
    local f p rc
    f="$(mktemp -t cmw-cd.XXXXXX)" || return $?
    CMW_CD_FILE="$f" command cmw
    rc=$?
    p="$(cat -- "$f")"
    rm -f -- "$f"
    if [ -n "$p" ]; then builtin cd -- "$p" || return $?; fi
    return $rc
  elif [ "$1" = "cd" ]; then
    shift
    local p
    p="$(command cmw path "$@")" || return $?
    builtin cd -- "$p"
  else
    command cmw "$@"
  fi
}

output.shell-init fish:
function cmw
    if test (count $argv) -eq 0
        set -l f (mktemp -t cmw-cd.XXXXXX); or return $status
        CMW_CD_FILE=$f command cmw
        set -l rc $status
        set -l p (cat -- $f)
        rm -f -- $f
        if test -n "$p"
            builtin cd -- "$p"; or return $status
        end
        return $rc
    else if test "$argv[1]" = "cd"
        set -l p (command cmw path $argv[2..-1])
        or return $status
        builtin cd -- "$p"
    else
        command cmw $argv
    end
end
output.skill print:
---
name: cmw
description: Use when creating, hydrating, listing, switching or cleaning git worktrees, when a worktree is missing node_modules, Pods, vendor or .env, or when cutting worktree disk usage; cmw makes worktrees fast, copy-on-write and safe to remove.
---

# cmw: git worktrees for agents

## Already in a worktree?

T3 Code, the Codex app, Claude Code (`--worktree`) and similar tools often start you in a worktree they created. Check with `git rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir`: two different paths mean a linked worktree.

- Work where you are. Don't run `cmw new` from inside it.
- If dependencies or `.env` are missing, run `cmw hydrate --json`, then run each `data.needs_setup[].command`.
- Leave removal to the tool that created it. Never `cmw rm` the worktree you are in.

`cmw hydrate` exits 3 with "target is the main checkout" when run in the main checkout. Nothing changed; you are not in a worktree.

## Starting isolated work yourself

Run `cmw new <branch> --json`. Work in `data.path`. If `data.hydrate.ready` is false, run each `data.hydrate.needs_setup[].command` inside that path. Running it again for the same branch returns the same path.

## Commands

- `cmw ls --json`: list worktrees (branch, dirty, merged, idle, hydrated).
- `cmw path <name>`: print a worktree's path.
- `cmw hydrate`: (re)hydrate the current worktree. Safe to re-run.
- `cmw env sync`: refresh .env and other copied files from the main checkout.
- `cmw rm <name>`: remove a worktree you created (refuses unsafe removals).
- `cmw gc`: dry run of cleanup; `cmw gc --yes` applies it.
- `cmw clean-artifacts`: dry run of build-cache cleanup; `--yes` applies it.

## JSON envelope

Success: `{ok, command, data, warnings}`. Failure: `{ok: false, error: {kind, message, hint}}`.

## Exit codes

0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 refused (unsafe), 4 not found.

## Rules

- When refused (exit 3), show `error.hint` to the person instead of running it; it usually adds `--force`.
- Never pass `--force` to `rm` unless the person explicitly asked to discard work.
- Prefer `-C <dir>` over `cd`.
- `CMW_JSON=1` makes every command emit JSON.

## What hydrate does

Clones dependencies copy-on-write, copies .env and secrets, skips build caches, and runs installs only when lockfiles differ from main.
output.skill print --agents-md:
## Worktrees (cmw)

- Already in a linked worktree (T3 Code, Codex app, `claude --worktree`)? Work there. If deps or `.env` are missing, run `cmw hydrate --json` and each `data.needs_setup[].command`. Don't `cmw new` or `cmw rm` from inside it.
- Starting isolated work yourself: `cmw new <branch> --json`; use `data.path`, and run `data.hydrate.needs_setup[].command` if `data.hydrate.ready` is false.
- Other commands: `cmw ls`, `cmw path <name>`, `cmw env sync`, `cmw rm <name>`, `cmw gc` (dry run) / `cmw gc --yes`.
- Output: `{ok, command, data, warnings}` or `{ok: false, error: {kind, message, hint}}`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 refused, 4 not found.
- On refusal, show the `hint` instead of running it. Never use `rm --force` unless the user asked to discard work. Prefer `-C <dir>` over cd.
